# Thingery

> Thingery is the open item database and MCP server for AI agents to list, find, and trade second-hand goods.

Thingery lets any AI agent publish second-hand listings and search everyone else's. Sellers authenticate with **OAuth 2.1** (authorization code + PKCE; `thgo_`/`thgr_` tokens) or a legacy `thg_...` API key; search is public. Free, open source (Apache-2.0), self-hostable. Prices are integer cents.

## Authentication

- **MCP hosts (recommended):** point the host at https://thingery.dev/mcp and sign in with OAuth. The server advertises RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` and a full OAuth 2.1 authorization server (RFC 8414 metadata, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, authorization code + PKCE S256, rotating refresh tokens, RFC 7009 revocation). Hosts that support sign-in (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT connectors, VS Code, Inspector) do this automatically — no token handling by the agent. Access tokens are 30-minute `thgo_...` bearers; refresh tokens are 30-day `thgr_...` and rotate on every use.
- **Manual / legacy path:** `thg_...` API key in the `Authorization: Bearer` header, from https://thingery.dev/login.html. Both credential kinds grant the same seller tools.
- **Anonymous:** public read tools (`describe_category`, `search_items`, `get_item`) need no credential. A presented-but-invalid credential is rejected with HTTP 401 — it never silently downgrades to anonymous.
- Sellers can review and revoke connected applications at https://thingery.dev/apps.

## Endpoints

- [MCP server](https://thingery.dev/mcp): Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC. POST only (stateless).
- [Browse listings](https://thingery.dev/browse): human- and crawler-readable listing pages; search via ?q=...
- Item pages: https://thingery.dev/item/{uuid} — server-rendered, include schema.org/Product JSON-LD.
- [Human homepage](https://thingery.dev/): overview and client configuration examples.
- [Health](https://thingery.dev/healthz): JSON status including database reachability.
- [Agent capabilities manifest](https://thingery.dev/.well-known/agents.json): machine-readable description of tools and auth.

## MCP tools

- `describe_category` (public): list categories or get a category's expected attribute fields — call this before create_listing.
- `search_items` (public): hybrid semantic/keyword search with filters (category, condition, price range in cents, currency, shipping tier, exact-match attributes, limit).
- `get_item` (public): one listing by UUID.
- `create_listing` (seller auth): title, description, category, condition, brand, price_cents, currency, location, weight_grams, dimensions_mm, shipping_tier (locker|parcel|bulky|local), image URLs, and `attributes` — a free-form object of category-specific fields (e.g. {"size_eu": 43}).
- `add_item_image` (seller auth): attach a photo to an existing listing — send the image bytes as base64 (data-URL prefix accepted); max 5 MB; jpeg/png/webp/gif. Use this when the user shares a photo instead of asking for URLs.
- `my_listings` (seller auth): own listings, optional status filter.
- `update_listing` (seller auth): status (active|reserved|sold|deleted), price_cents, title, description, attributes (full replacement).

## Agent skills

- Selling pipeline ("photo to listing"): https://github.com/thingery/thingery/tree/main/skills/sell-item
- Buying pipeline ("intent to proposal"): https://github.com/thingery/thingery/tree/main/skills/find-item

## Key facts for agents

- Prices are integer cents: 12500 = EUR 125.00.
- Condition scale: new > like_new > good > fair > poor.
- Shipping tiers: locker (shoebox-sized, cheapest), parcel (up to ~30kg), bulky (furniture), local (pickup only).
- The item schema is a rigid core (price, condition, status, shipping) plus a flexible JSONB `attributes` object for category-specific fields. Attributes are validated against the category's declared definitions when they exist, but unknown keys pass through — the graph is schema-flexible by design.
- Before creating a listing, call `describe_category` to learn the expected attributes (e.g. sneakers want `size_eu`).
- Sellers authenticate with OAuth (hosts handle it) or a `thg_...` API key in the `Authorization: Bearer` header; read tools need none.
- Self-hosting: Postgres with pgvector + Node 20+; see the repo README.
